title: The assassination
description: On June 28, 1914, when Gavrilo Princip, a 19-year-old Bosnian Serb, shot Archduke Franz Ferdinand of Austria and his wife Sophie at this corner. The murder led within weeks to the First World War.
spotify: Dan Snow's History Hit Sarajevo 1914: Assassination of the Archduke
apple: Dan Snow's History Hit Sarajevo 1914: Assassination of the Archduke

title: A book that survived two wars
place: National Museum of Bosnia and Herzegovina
description: On the Sarajevo Haggadah, an illustrated Jewish prayer book made in Spain in the 1300s. A Muslim librarian hid it from the Nazis, and it was saved again during the siege. It is kept in the National Museum.

title: The Jews of Sarajevo
place: Museum of the Jews of Bosnia and Herzegovina
description: The story of Sarajevo’s Jews, most of them descended from those expelled from Spain in 1492, who arrived in the 1500s. Most were killed in the Holocaust. The old synagogue, from 1581, is now their museum.
spotify: Remembering Yugoslavia The Jews of Sarajevo
apple: Remembering Yugoslavia The Jews of Sarajevo

title: The siege
episode: The Bosnian War Part II-The Siege of Sarajevo
description: On the siege of Sarajevo, from April 1992 to February 1996, when Bosnian Serb forces in the hills shelled the city and shot at its people. Two of its first victims were killed on this bridge at a peace march.
spotify: Reflecting History The Bosnian War Part II-The Siege of Sarajevo
apple: Reflecting History The Bosnian War Part II-The Siege of Sarajevo

title: Theater under siege
episode: Still Waiting for Godot in Sarajevo?
description: BBC correspondent Allan Little, who reported on the siege, returns to ask what became of the culture that kept going during it. In 1993 the American writer Susan Sontag staged Waiting for Godot in this theater, by candlelight.

apple: The Documentary Podcast: Archive 2014 Still Waiting for Godot in Sarajevo?

title: Childhood in wartime
episode: A Sarajevo Museum Gives Children Of War A Voice
description: On the War Childhood Museum, founded by a man who grew up in the siege. It shows objects given by people who were children then, each with their own short story: a doll, a diary, a pair of ballet shoes.
